closes.text: FIXED AS RULED. The case now asserts on the SERVER's count: `std::http::refused_body_census()` - an `[internal]` instrument on both backends (`__http_refused_body_census`) that counts body bytes the server took off a connection after deciding not to read the body (a 413 refusal, or a body left unread past the cap); it counts, it decides nothing. The pin reads the census before and after the 64 MiB writer and requires zero; the client side keeps a secondary check with no figure (the write fails, or the server's FIN or reset is read). Node is hardened on the way: it stops reading at the REFUSAL (pause + readStop; `resume`/`_read` inert for the half second left) rather than at the answer's flush. The Windows+Node leg stays strict. The flake was not reproduced (Windows-only; Linux reads 0); the pin is plant-proven on both legs - a draining Node server read 63,432,536 bytes, a native server that keeps reading read 63,340,928 - and the CI job that will show it is `test (windows-latest, 2, 4)`. If Windows Node really keeps reading, the census will now say so with the server's own count. Three recurrences recorded (56 MiB, 26.7 MiB, 64 MiB).
